commitResults.messageTitle: List acknowledgements in the Developer Guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The Acknowledgements section still held the AB3 authoring instruction
instead of naming the sources.

Let's list AB3, the libraries, PlantUML and the AI tools used, each
with a link to the original.

The Saving data tests still ended with the AB3 placeholder, and the
Launch and shutdown items were numbered 2. to 4. instead of 1. as the
Markdown conventions require.

Let's remove the placeholder and number every item 1.

The AB3 undo/redo proposal treated a delete preview as a deletion,
captioned a diagram with the removed list command, and ended with an
authoring placeholder.

TutorTrack has no undo/redo design, so let's remove the section and
the diagrams that only it used.

commitResults.messageTitle: Align the v2 student archiving scope in both guides
commitResults.messageBody:
The User Guide promised data-file archiving in v2.0 with no details,
and the Developer Guide held only an authoring placeholder.

Let's describe the planned student archiving feature as coming soon in
the User Guide, and its proposed design in the Developer Guide.

commitResults.messageTitle: Replace the add-student sequence diagram with an activity diagram
commitResults.messageBody:
The add-student sequence diagram showed parser and command internals
that made the main flow hard to follow.

Let's show the successful path as an activity diagram with one
swimlane per component, and update the Developer Guide text to match.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document that commands and prefixes must be lowercase
commitResults.messageBody:
The command-format notes did not say that command words and prefixes
are case-sensitive, and add, edit and edit note did not say what a
wrong-case prefix does. The Developer Guide did not record the
decision.

Let's state the rule in the notes box, describe the current
wrong-case results beside each command, and record the decision and
its reason in the Developer Guide.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix small User Guide and Developer Guide wording issues
commitResults.messageBody:
Neither guide explained the roster sort order or what happens to a
data file edited while TutorTrack runs, and the User Guide did not
warn about two windows. Fixing command errors repeated details of
each command, add used bold labels unlike other commands, some
paragraphs ran past four sentences, and the FAQ had one entry.

Let's document the sort order and the two data-file cases, keep only
general hints in Fixing command errors and move the rest beside each
command, match the add bullets to other commands, split long
paragraphs, and add common questions to the FAQ.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reorganize the Developer Guide implementation section
commitResults.messageBody:
The implementation section mixed command routing, student identity,
UI behaviour and session-note internals, the UI component was written
as long prose, and several paragraphs ran to nine sentences.

Let's order the sections as student storage and identity, display,
session notes, then each command, write the UI component as bullets,
and split every paragraph to at most four sentences without changing
its wording.

The Developer Guide still had AB3 placeholders: an empty
Acknowledgements section, an unrelated undo/redo proposal, and
"more test cases" and data archiving stubs.

Let's,
* list AB3, the libraries, PlantUML and the AI tools used
* remove the undo/redo walkthrough and its nine diagrams
* remove the manual-testing placeholder and number the launch items
* describe student archiving as Coming soon in the UG, with its
  proposed design in the DG

The add sequence diagram was too detailed, wrong-case input was not
documented, several UG sections were long or vague, and the DG
implementation section had no clear order.

Let's,
* replace the add sequence diagram with an activity diagram of the
  successful path, with one swimlane per component
* state that command words, prefixes, note and /confirm must be
  lowercase, and describe what wrong-case input does in each command
* explain the roster sort order, add six FAQ entries and a known
  issue for running two windows, and move error details into each
  command's section
* reorder the DG implementation section and split long paragraphs
